sense: something that helps bring about a result

terms.gloss: a factor, something that tips the balance; weight, influence
evidence: Liv. 21.4.2: ut pater in sē minimum mōmentum ad favōrem conciliandum esset
Caes. BC 3.70: ita parvae rēs magnum in utramque partem mōmentum habuērunt
terms.comment: Properly the weight that tips a balance, and so a circumstance that decides an outcome: magnum mōmentum habēre, to be a big factor. Lewis & Short: “a cause, a circumstance; weight, influence, importance”. Of time, a moment (see moment).

terms.gloss: count for something in, be a factor in
terms.grammar: phrase: valeō with ad and the accusative, often a gerund
evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.182: valet igitur multum ad vincendum probārī mōrēs … eōrum, quī agent causās
Cic. Phil. 9.12: multum valuisse ad patris honōrem pietās fīliī vidēbitur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Multum valet ad, it is a big factor in; nihil valet ad, it plays no part in.

terms.gloss: a cause, one of the reasons
terms.comment: See reason and cause: in causā esse, to be a cause (Livy).

phrases.latin: dein brevī effēcit, ut pater in sē minimum mōmentum ad favōrem conciliandum esset
phrases.english: soon he made his father the least of the factors that won him favour

phrases.latin: quod saepe in bellō parvīs mōmentīs magnī cāsūs intercēderent
phrases.english: because in war great reversals often turn on small factors

phrases.latin: Minimīs mōmentīs, patrēs cōnscrīptī, maximae inclīnātiōnēs temporum fīunt
phrases.english: The greatest turns of fortune, senators, come about through the smallest factors

sources: Lewis & Short: momentum · Lewis & Short: valeo · Lewis & Short: causa
